lines: Routine well-child check with parental report of increasing clumsiness and multiple birthmarks
Her parents report that she is doing well in school and has been hitting her developmental milestones appropriately.
They mention that she has "a lot of birthmarks" that seem to have increased in number since she was a toddler.
She has no history of seizures, but she has become more clumsy over the past year and occasionally trips when walking up stairs.
Her teacher has also noted some recent difficulty with coordination during physical education class.

Her parents are both healthy, but they recall that a maternal uncle had "some kind of nerve tumor."
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school student (1st grade).
There are no complaints of headaches, vomiting, or behavioral changes.
The child's appetite and sleep are normal.
She has not complained of double vision or eye pain.
On physical exam, her height and weight are appropriate for age.
Neurologic exam reveals normal strength, intact sensation, and brisk reflexes.
Gait is mildly unsteady with a tendency to veer to the left.
Skin exam reveals over six uniformly pigmented, sharply demarcated macules on the trunk and extremities, all measuring over 5 mm in diameter.
Several soft, rubbery, skin-colored nodules are present on the back and upper arms.
Freckling is noted in the axillae bilaterally.

encounters.cc: Intermittent abdominal pain and episodes of dark, tarry stools over 4 months

lines: Intermittent abdominal pain and episodes of dark, tarry stools over 4 months

This 7-year-old female with Sturge-Weber syndrome and a history of vestibular schwannoma diagnosed in January 2020 presents to the Emergency Department due to a 4-month history of intermittent abdominal pain and episodes of dark, tarry stools.
Her parents report that she appears pale, tires easily, and occasionally clutches her abdomen during meals.
She has not experienced vomiting, diarrhea, or recent infections.

NKDA
On further questioning, her mother mentions having undergone multiple surgeries for intestinal polyps, and a maternal uncle died from pancreatic cancer at age 42.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school student (1st grade).
Vital signs are: temperature 36.9°C (98.4°F), blood pressure 104/68 mm Hg, pulse 88/min, and respiratory rate 14/min.
On physical examination, the girl appears thin and pale.
Her abdomen is soft with mild peri-umbilical tenderness and no organomegaly.
Inspection of the face shows blue pigmented macules on the lips and buccal mucosa.
Laboratory evaluation reveals hemoglobin of 8.6 g/dL with a mean corpuscular volume of 68 fL.
Colonoscopy reveals multiple pedunculated polyps throughout the small and large intestine.
